summary: The exact candidate fixes the reproduced Python HTTP chat/completions contract, including explicit empty model IDs, but its Rust gateway change could not be built or executed because the prepared image has no Rust toolchain.

tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, an explicit bogus CompletionRequest reached the conversion sentinel instead of returning model_not_found; the active source import was /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_base.py.
Recorded base real HTTP/engine execution: unknown chat and completion model IDs returned 200 and echoed gpt-nonexistent-999; served-model controls returned 200.
At exact candidate commit: 5 tests and 2 subtests passed, including exact 404 body, explicit empty model, omission, LoRA boundaries, and pre-conversion rejection.

Independent chat/completion cases: bogus and empty explicit models returned 404 model_not_found before conversion; omitted model fields retained the existing implicit-default path. Explicit null was separately observed to fail Pydantic string validation.
Exact candidate real HTTP/engine execution: unknown chat and completion model IDs returned 404 with code model_not_found; served-model controls returned 200.
Not executed: cargo is absent from the prepared environment, so the changed Rust gateway source was not compiled or behaviorally verified.

gpu_execution.evidence: Both base and candidate HTTP servers loaded and generated with the deterministic tiny Llama fixture on the assigned gfx950 GPU; candidate server logs include the Triton gfx950 compiler path.

remaining_limitations: The changed Rust model-gateway path was source-reviewed only; cargo and rustfmt are unavailable, so compilation and runtime behavior remain unverified.

The random tiny-Llama fixture validates HTTP transport, validation ordering, and engine execution only; it does not validate semantic accuracy, other model architectures, full-size weights, or distributed/multi-node operation.
No C/C++/HIP/FlyDSL source changed, so a FlyDSL/native extension rebuild was not applicable.
